entry_state: Pension availability depends on enforceable refund and funding terms, and restoration cash classification depends on the paid activity with competing interpretations retained. Group impairment tests units before wider groups using adjusted balances. The partial-goodwill discussion distinguishes notional test amounts from recognized goodwill and losses; its larger-unit allocation has been read through page 148 and remains open pending the next transition.
exit_state: Group impairment, partial goodwill and tax calculations preserve their distinct populations and origins. Revaluation-related tax follows profit/OCI history; acquisition and outside-basis tax have different recognition tests, and Pillar Two uses the inspected exception. The new useful-life case has introduced two different histories: newly arising restrictions versus an original documented six-year life transcribed as twelve. Its date and statement consequences continue next.
findings: The partial-goodwill cases distinguish unrecognized NCI goodwill from recognized parent goodwill and separately allocate identifiable-asset losses.
Revalued impairment retains the profit/OCI origin of tax and does not assume offset presentation or actual tax law.
Acquisition and outside-basis examples state asymmetric recognition conditions; the Pillar Two amendment supplies an accounting exception, not a computed company tax liability.
The useful-life comparison starts from different information histories, not two elective treatments for the same facts. No new confirmed defect.
